A rectangular box measuring $8$ by $6$ by $4$ has a cylindrical hole (radius $2$, drilled fully through the height of $4$) removed. Find the remaining volume, in terms of $\pi$.
questions.answer: Box volume $=8\times6\times4=192$. Cylinder removed $=\pi(4)(4)=16\pi$. Remaining volume $=192-16\pi$.

questions.q: A solid consists of a cylinder (radius $4$, height $8$) topped by a hemisphere of the same radius. Find the total volume, in terms of $\pi$.
A solid is a rectangular box ($10$ by $6$ by $5$) with a square pyramid (base $6$ by $6$, height $4$) carved out of the top. Find the remaining volume.
questions.answer: Box: $10\times6\times5=300$. Pyramid: $\dfrac{1}{3}(36)(4)=48$. Remaining volume $=300-48=252$ cubic units.

questions.q: Two similar cylinders have heights $6$ and $9$. Find the ratio of their volumes.
Two similar spheres have surface areas in the ratio $9:25$. Find the ratio of their volumes.
A scale model of a statue is built at a $1:20$ scale. The actual statue has volume $4000$ m$^3$. Find the volume of the model.
Two similar rectangular boxes have volumes in the ratio $8:27$. Find the ratio of their surface areas.
questions.answer: Volume ratio $=k^3=\dfrac{8}{27}\Rightarrow k=\dfrac{2}{3}$. Surface area ratio $=k^2=\dfrac{4}{9}$.

questions.q: A cone has base radius $8$. A plane parallel to the base slices the cone at half the height, measured from the apex. Find the radius of the circular cross-section at that height.
questions.answer: The cross-section radius scales linearly with distance from the apex: radius $=8\times\dfrac{1}{2}=4$.

questions.q: A cube of side $12$ is sliced by a plane through the midpoints of the three edges meeting at one vertex. Find the area of the resulting triangular cross-section.
questions.answer: Each cut edge has length $6$ (half of $12$), and the two cut edges at each pair meet at a right angle, so each side of the triangular cross-section has length $\sqrt{6^2+6^2}=6\sqrt{2}$. By symmetry the triangle is equilateral, so its area is $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(6\sqrt{2})^2=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(72)=18\sqrt{3}$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: a grain silo

questions.q: This question has three parts. A grain silo is shaped like a cylinder topped with a cone, both with radius $5$ m. The cylindrical part has height $12$ m, and the conical roof has height $3$ m. Use $\pi\approx3.14159$. (a) Find the total volume of the silo (cylinder plus cone), to the nearest cubic meter. (b) The silo is filled with grain up to the top of the cylindrical part only. If each cubic meter of grain has a mass of $750$ kg, find the total mass of grain stored, to the nearest kilogram. (c) A second, similar silo is built at $1.4$ times the linear scale of the first, in every dimension. Find the volume of the second silo, to the nearest cubic meter.
questions.answer: (a) Cylinder: $\pi(25)(12)=300\pi\approx942.48$ m$^3$. Cone: $\dfrac{1}{3}\pi(25)(3)=25\pi\approx78.54$ m$^3$. Total $\approx1021.02$, so $1021$ m$^3$. (b) Cylinder volume $\approx942.48$ m$^3$. Mass $\approx942.48\times750\approx706858$ kg. (c) Volume scales as $k^3=1.4^3=2.744$. New volume $\approx1021.02\times2.744\approx2802$ m$^3$.
